domain: Labor Relations / Institutional Control / Debt Bondage
topic_summary: Analysis of a narrative depicting migrant labor exploitation on Mars, where a worker is manipulated into informant activity through false promises of collective improvement, then punished for the very activities he was encouraged to perform. The story demonstrates how institutional control operates through manufactured complicity and debt leverage.

key_entities: Miguel Santos (protagonist; outer-ring lithium extraction worker; 33 months into 40-month contract)
Supervisor Reyes (compliance intelligence officer posing as worker advocate)
Dante (Miguel's bunkmate; actual organizer who is neutralized through Miguel's informant activity)
Rosa/Family (debt leverage; house construction funded by signing bonus)
The Contract (legal instrument defining prohibited activities and liability terms)
key_tensions: Worker solidarity vs institutional infiltration (Dante's organizing vs Reyes's intelligence operation)
Debt obligation vs labor rights (family financial dependence vs exploitative contract terms)
Perceived agency vs structural coercion (Miguel's 'choices' vs predetermined outcomes)

axes.structural_delta: Financial obligations to dependents transform worker resistance into institutional compliance through manufactured consent
axes.primary_observable: Ratio of signing bonus liability to household income; frequency of family-welfare justifications for compliance decisions
axes.selection_reason: Upstream structural constraint enabling both downstream dynamics; different observable from other axes (financial liability vs behavioral manipulation)

axes.structural_delta: Authority figures adopt worker identity markers to elicit trust, then extract intelligence under pretense of collective action
axes.primary_observable: Frequency of shared identity signaling by authority figures; ratio of 'organizing' meetings that result in worker reassignments vs actual collective action
axes.selection_reason: Central synthesis node; highest centrality score; distinct beneficiary/victim structure from upstream axis

axes.structural_delta: Institutional agents induce prohibited behavior through authority directives, then prosecute the induced behavior as voluntary contract violation
axes.primary_observable: Presence of institutional encouragement in case files vs acknowledgment of that encouragement in tribunal proceedings; contract liability enforcement rate for intelligence-operation participants vs organic violators
axes.selection_reason: Downstream synthesis node; highest centrality; captures the terminal extraction mechanism where both upstream dynamics converge

axes.structural_delta: Physical segregation by contract tier creates visible gradient of material conditions, channeling worker aspiration toward individual advancement rather than collective action
axes.primary_observable: Correlation between hab-ring assignment and compliance behavior; frequency of promotion-as-reward in worker narratives
axes.selection_reason: Deferred: lower centrality; spatial mechanism is context for informant recruitment but not structurally independent from it

axes.structural_delta: Unspecified punishment protocols generate compliance through fear of unknown consequences rather than known penalties
axes.primary_observable: Ratio of workers who know processing details vs workers who modify behavior to avoid it; variance in post-processing testimony
axes.selection_reason: Deferred: terminal enforcement mechanism but structurally downstream of snare; opacity is implementation detail of retroactive criminalization

deferred_axes.structural_delta: Physical segregation channels aspiration toward individual advancement rather than collective action
deferred_axes.deferral_reason: Lower centrality; spatial mechanism provides context for informant recruitment but lacks structural independence

omegas.description: Is Supervisor Reyes a willing agent of institutional control (beneficiary) or herself a coerced informant one tier up? Her 11-year tenure and middle-ring position suggest either genuine advancement or long-term entrapment. Classification affects whether informant_recruitment is pure tangled_rope or nested snare.
omegas.source: Dark Matter Probe 3 (Beneficiary Scan) + narrative ambiguity regarding Reyes's motivations

omegas.description: Dante's fate after giving names is unspecified. If he was also prosecuted for organizing, the snare operates symmetrically on both organizers and informants. If he was merely reassigned, the extraction is asymmetric (informants punished, organizers neutralized but not prosecuted).
omegas.source: Absence Inventory (§1.1) + narrative gap in Dante's post-reassignment status

omegas.description: The tribunal's rejection of 'misunderstanding or coercion' claims suggests contract terms override institutional inducement. But is this legally enforceable on Earth, or does Mars's jurisdictional isolation enable contract terms that would be void elsewhere? Affects whether this is rope (coordination failure) or mountain (legal regime).
omegas.source: F34 (Epistemic Trespass) + legal domain beyond model's competence

omegas.description: The 72-hour processing protocol is deliberately opaque in the narrative. Is it psychological conditioning, physical coercion, memory alteration, or administrative detention? The mechanism matters for classifying whether deterrence operates through known consequences (rope) or unknown terror (piton).
omegas.source: Deferred axis processing_as_deterrence_through_opacity + narrative deliberate ambiguity

fracture_scan.notes: F34 detected: Contract enforceability and jurisdictional questions exceed model's legal domain competence. Generated omega_contract_enforceability to bound this uncertainty. All three selected axes operate at the behavioral/institutional level where model competence is adequate.
